evals.prompt: I'm kicking off a B2B invoicing dashboard for accountants. Before I build anything I want the foundational design variables set up — colors, fonts, spacing, the works — with a dark mode. Can you generate the tokens and a Tailwind theme into a ./design folder?
evals.expected_output: Runs the design-tokens generator with a dense/dashboard density, produces tokens.css (light + dark CSS custom properties, type scale, spacing, radii, shadows), tailwind.config.js, and a README, then summarizes the chosen style, palette, and font pairing.

assertions.text: A tokens.css file is produced containing :root CSS custom properties
tokens.css defines a dark theme via both prefers-color-scheme and a [data-theme="dark"] or .dark selector
A tailwind.config.js is produced that references the CSS variables (var(--color-...))
The response summarizes the chosen palette and font pairing to the user

evals.prompt: generate a tailwind theme + css variables for a calm meditation app, spacious feel, needs to look good in dark mode
evals.expected_output: Runs the generator with a low density (spacious), produces the token files with a soft/calm style, and reports the palette and dark theme.

assertions.text: The spacing scale reflects a spacious (low-density) setting
tokens.css includes a dark theme block
A tailwind.config.js with fontFamily heading/body mapped to CSS variables is produced

evals.prompt: Set up the design system foundations (palette, type scale, radii, shadows, spacing) for a bold brutalist portfolio site for a graphic designer. I want it opinionated.
evals.expected_output: Runs the generator with high variance, producing brutalist tokens: zero radii and hard offset shadows, a dramatic type ratio, plus the CSS variables and Tailwind config.

assertions.text: The radii tokens are 0px, matching a brutalist style
The shadow tokens are hard offset shadows rather than soft blurs
tokens.css and tailwind.config.js are both produced
